en.text: Physics supports every other science: chemistry (atoms, heat, spectra), biology (balance, fluids, sound, nerves, light), astronomy (gravity, light, spectra), geology (waves, magnetism), engineering and technology, medicine (X-ray, CT, MRI, ultrasound, radiotherapy), defence (radar R = ct/2, infrared) and communication (electromagnetic waves).

screens.title: Warm up: where is this physics used?
Unit summary
paras: Sciences depend on and reinforce each other.
Chemistry is rooted in atomic and molecular physics.
Biology uses mechanics, fluids, sound, electricity and light.
Astronomers use light, atomic physics and Newton's laws.
Medical devices like X-ray, MRI, CT and ultrasound come from physics.
Radar and infrared night vision use electromagnetic waves.

screens.title: Key word
defs: The use of physics to diagnose and treat disease.

screens.title: Match the device to its physics
screens.why:
X-ray: tissues absorb X-rays by different amounts.
MRI: hydrogen nuclei line up in a strong magnet.
Ultrasound: echoes of high-frequency sound.
Radar: radio echoes; range R = ct/2.
Night vision: infrared given off by warm bodies.
screens.clue: Think of what each one sends or detects.
screens.text: Unit 1 review: match each device to the physics it uses.
End of unit Q1, energy in biology: in photosynthesis, energy changes from
screens.why:
Plants absorb sunlight (light energy).
They use it to make glucose.
Glucose stores the energy as chemical energy.
So light → chemical.

screens.text: End of unit Q8, medical devices: a diagnostic device differs from a therapeutic one because it
screens.why:
Diagnostic devices look inside to find what is wrong (X-ray, MRI, ultrasound).
Therapeutic devices treat the disease (radiotherapy).
Answer: it finds out what is wrong.

screens.ask: Radar range: an echo returns after 2.0 ms. The target is ___ km away
screens.why:
Formula: R = ct/2.
Convert: t = 2.0 ms = 2.0 × 10⁻³ s.
Substitute: R = 3 × 10⁸ × 2.0 × 10⁻³ / 2 = 3 × 10⁵ m.
Result: 300 km.
Trap: forgetting ÷2 gives 600 km.

items.text: End of unit Q1, physics in biology: how does the brain get information from the body?
items.why:
Sense organs turn stimuli into signals.
Sensory neurons carry them to the brain as electrical pulses.
Motor neurons carry pulses from the brain to the muscles.
Answer: neurons carry electrical pulses.

items.text: End of unit Q1, physics in medicine: a clinical thermometer works by
opts: expansion of a liquid (or a thermistor)
items.ans: expansion of a liquid (or a thermistor)
items.why:
Heat flows from the body into the thermometer.
It stops when both reach the same temperature (thermal equilibrium).
The liquid expands with temperature and rises in the tube.
Digital thermometers use a thermistor instead.

items.text: End of unit Q2: which physics is used in designing a modern car? Pick all that apply.
items.why:
Newton's laws: acceleration, braking and safety.
Aerodynamics: shaping the body to cut air drag.
Pascal's principle: hydraulic brakes pass pressure to every wheel.
Radioactive dating finds the age of old objects, not car design.

items.text: End of unit Q3: why is the physics of light important in astronomy?
opts: Light is almost the only information we get from far objects
items.ans: Light is almost the only information we get from far objects
items.why:
Stars and galaxies are far too far to visit.
Almost all we learn comes from the light (radiation) they send.
Spectral lines in that light show composition and temperature.

items.text: End of unit Q9: which are uses of radar? Pick all that apply.
items.why:
Air traffic control: radar finds planes and their distance.
Weather: radar echoes from rain show storms.
Ships: radar finds coasts and other ships in fog.
Body temperature is measured with a thermometer, not radar.

items.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about reflection and refraction of sound waves and their applications?
opts: A. Reflection and refraction of sound are used to detect flaws in metals and to help people park their cars.
B. Refraction of sound is the change in its direction as it travels through a medium having different densities.
C. In pre-natal scanning, reflection and refraction of sound allows doctors to monitor the progress of a developing body.
D. Reflection of sound (echo) is formed when sound enters a medium of varying densities.
items.ans: D. Reflection of sound (echo) is formed when sound enters a medium of varying densities.
items.why:
Reflection (echo): sound bounces back from a boundary or surface.
Refraction: sound changes direction as it passes into regions of different density.
D describes refraction but calls it reflection, so D is NOT correct.
A is true: flaw detectors and parking sensors use echoes.
B is the correct definition of refraction.
C is true: pre-natal scans use echoes from tissue boundaries.

items.text: An FM radio signal is transmitted from a radio station at a frequency of 1.5×10⁸ Hz. If the wavelength of the radio wave is 2.00 m, the speed of the FM signal is
items.why:
Formula: v = fλ.
Substitute: v = 1.5 × 10⁸ Hz × 2.00 m.
Result: v = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s, the speed of light, as expected for a radio wave.
Trap: B divides f by λ; D divides λ by f; C doubles the answer.

test.text: Physics and chemistry: both sciences study
test.why:
Physics studies matter, energy and their interaction.
Chemistry studies matter and how it changes, which involves energy.
So both study matter and energy.

CT = computerized tomography.
"Tomography" means imaging in slices.
A computer builds the slices from many X-ray views.

test.text: Medical ultrasound: hospital ultrasound scanners use about
test.why:
Ultrasound is above 20 kHz.
Medical scanners use 3.5–10 MHz.
Trap: 3.5–10 Hz has the right numbers but the wrong unit.

test.ask: Radar range: the echo returns after 0.1 ms. Range = ___ km
test.why:
Formula: R = ct/2.
Convert: t = 0.1 ms = 1 × 10⁻⁴ s.
R = 3 × 10⁸ × 1 × 10⁻⁴ / 2 = 1.5 × 10⁴ m.
Result: 15 km.
